digest.en: Asia-Pacific leads the board this hour with China’s disputed satellite refueling heralds new space war era. Europe & Russia carries the next thread. 25 fresh dispatches in this edition.

articles.title: China’s disputed satellite refueling heralds new space war era
articles.summary: Recent disclosures about China’s purported in-orbit servicing operations have intensified a quiet revolution in space, where the mechanics of satellite sustainment are swiftly becoming the frontline of great-power counterspace rivalry. articles.summary: Volkswagen has spent years trying to build a European battery business strong enough to carry its electric-car ambitions. articles.summary: Iran’s seven-day plan envisages an end to all hostilities in Iran and Lebanon, the unfreezing of billions of dollars’ ‌worth of Iranian assets, an end to sanctions on Iranian oil and the lifting of the US blockade on Iranian ports. articles.title: Why Israel banned Arab parties ahead of polls

articles.title: Malaysia starts sending Myanmar migrants home
articles.summary: Dozens of buses arrived under police escort at the Majlis Perbandaran Manjung stadium near the Lumut naval base in northwestern Malaysia. The migrants were expected to be processed before being taken to Myanmar by ship. Malaysia starts sending Myanmar migrants home.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Warns Of New Russian Mobilization, 10,000 North Korean Troop Deployment
articles.summary: The death toll from Russia’s jet-powered drone attacks mounted in Ukraine while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that the Kremlin is preparing for a new mobilization at home and a fresh deployment of 10,000 North Korean troops. articles.title: Deadly Russian Attacks On Ukraine Hit Medical Center, Science Academy
articles.summary: Russian forces struck civilian sites on 28 September, setting fire to the National Academy of Sciences and a major medical clinic in Kyiv. An office building in Dnipro and an apartment block in Kharkiv also suffered damage. The attacks caused casualties and disrupted services. A wave of Russian attacks hit civilian sites in several Ukrainian cities on September 28. In Kyiv, fire broke out after strikes on the National Academy of Sciences and a major medical clinic.

articles.title: Kallas Says Russia's Mockery Of UN Meeting Shows It's Not Interested In Ending Ukraine War
articles.summary: European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on September 28 that Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's treatment of his German counterpart, Johann Wadephul, after their recent UN meeting demonstrates that Russia is not interested in peace in Ukraine. Kallas Says Russia's Mockery Of UN Meeting Shows It's Not Interested In Ending Ukraine War.

articles.title: General Debate ends with call to turn words into action
articles.summary: After six days of speeches from the UN General Assembly podium, one word rose above all others: peace. This final edition of The Takeaway distils the messages he said reverberated through the Assembly Hall and looks at where the 193-member body goes from here. General Debate ends with call to turn words into action.

articles.title: UN leaders renew push to defeat racism, 25 years after Durban
articles.summary: “No country is free of racism.” That warning from US youth activist Marley Dias set the tone on Monday as UN Member States reinvigorated global efforts against racism, discrimination and xenophobia with a new declaration. UN leaders renew push to defeat racism, 25 years after Durban.

articles.title: DPR Korea tells UN its nuclear status is ‘irreversible’, rejects outside pressure
articles.summary: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) told the UN General Assembly on Monday that its status as a nuclear-armed State was irreversible, arguing that its military capabilities were necessary to safeguard the country’s sovereignty and maintain peace on the Korean Peninsula. DPR Korea tells UN its nuclear status is ‘irreversible’, rejects outside pressure.

articles.title: Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report
articles.summary: Support for water and sanitation at the biggest camp in the world for Syrian refugees is under threat from a lack of funding – combined with the impact of climate change – the UN Children’s Fund, UNICEF, said on Monday. Refugee funding, US migration policy triggers ‘cascade’ of rights violations, world forests report.

articles.title: Ambassadors meet as West Bank tensions rise, Gaza plan stalls
articles.summary: The Security Council met Monday morning with prospects for peace in the Middle East under strain on two fronts. In the West Bank, settler violence and settlement expansion are raising fears for a two-State solution. In Gaza, a year-old peace plan has stalled while civilian suffering continues. The meeting comes as the plan’s remaining phases, including Hamas’ disarmament and Israel’s full withdraw.

articles.title: World leaders take stock of global fight against racism
articles.summary: World leaders are meeting in the General Assembly to assess how far the world has come in combating racism and how far it still has to go. The Durban Declaration and Programme of Action, the most comprehensive framework of its kind, seeks to acknowledge historical injustices, dismantle inequalities and build societies grounded in dignity, equality and justice for all. World leaders take stock of global fight against racism.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access
articles.summary: Aid teams trying to keep deadly Ebola disease from spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are increasingly concerned about ongoing fighting and violence that has forced thousands of people to flee a displacement camp in the vast, resource-rich east of the country. DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access.

articles.summary: Hurricane Nolo is moving away from Hawaiian islands but threat of heavy rain, flash floods and strong winds persistsHurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms. articles.summary: As US President Donald Trump publicly rejected Iran’s proposal for a ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz this weekend, the Iranian foreign minister reiterated that “there is no alternative to a negotiated solution.” “There’s always hope for diplomacy,” though the Trump-led United States has been an untrustworthy negotiator, Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said during a Sunday appear Trump rejects deal, Iran diplomat calls for ‘negotiated solution’.

articles.title: Canada urges stronger partnerships as global order faces ‘rupture’
